svg.text: TLS 1.3 — Algorithm Roles in the PQC vs Classical Benchmark
Only Key Exchange and Digital Signature change between scenarios. AEAD and Hash are fixed by the cipher suite TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, so every scenario runs under identical symmetric conditions.
Establishes the shared secret (ECDHE or ML-KEM KEM).
Negotiated via signature_algorithms. Used in the Certificate
chain and in CertificateVerify (signed on every handshake).
Classical: ECDSA P-384 + SHA-384, ECDSA P-521 + SHA-512
AES-256-GCM encrypts and authenticates every record
SHA-384 drives the HKDF key schedule, the transcript
Why only KEX and SIG vary
Fixing the cipher suite isolates the cost of the asymmetric operations under test:
• Bytes on the wire: larger key shares, certificates and signatures in PQC scenarios
Symmetric cost (AES-256-GCM, SHA-384) is the same in every scenario,
so measured differences come from KEX + SIG only.
TEST SCENARIOS — what changes and what stays constant
same in A1 · A2 · B1 · C1 · C2
same in A1 · A2 · B1 · C1 · C2
In TLS 1.3 the cipher suite defines only the AEAD and the hash; key exchange (supported_groups) and signature (signature_algorithms) are negotiated separately.
The SHA-384 / SHA-512 in the ECDSA schemes, SHAKE in ML-DSA and SHA-2 in SLH-DSA belong to the signature scheme itself, not to the suite hash (always SHA-384).
TLS 1.3 has no separate record MAC: integrity comes from the AEAD.
